answer:
Yes, the handover is a documentable event, and the CRM already carries the pattern by scope note. What actually lies outside responsible assertion is narrower than the question fears, and it is not the informality.

1. The tractable handle is the role, not the right. E74 Group's scope note extends the class, in the wider sense, to official positions that are regarded in a given context as one actor independent of the current holder, and adds that such a group may never have had more than one member. So "the fire-keeper of the village midsummer bonfire" is an instance of E74 Group, distinct from the persons (E21) who have held it. Informality is inside the model by construction rather than tolerated at its edge: E66 Formation is explicitly about the formation of a formal or informal group, so if the custom's origin were ever recoverable it would have a class too.

2. The transfer is then two events the CRM names in its own scope notes. E85 Joining lists among its typical scenarios the inauguration of somebody into an official position, and gives the election of Newton to Parliament and Gorbachev's inauguration as examples; use P143 joined for the successor and P144 joined with for the position. E86 Leaving lists the end of tenure of somebody in an official position, with George Washington leaving office in 1797 as an example; use P145 separated for the predecessor and P146 separated from for the position. Both are subclasses of E7 Activity, so both take P14 carried out by (here the outgoing fire-keeper, who alone chooses the moment, which is exactly the active participation P14 records) and P4 has time-span. The unbroken chain the project wants is the P107 has current or former member set of the position, and P107 is declared to be a shortcut of precisely the path E74 Group, P144i gained member by, E85 Joining, P143 joined, E39 Actor. Chain and links are therefore the same statement at two levels of detail, which is what a heritage project needs. Keep Joining and Leaving as two events rather than collapsing them into one: this case needs them apart, because the private act and the community's coming to accept the successor over the following year or two are not the same moment and may deserve different bounds.

3. Undatedness is a case the model anticipates, not a defect. E52 Time-Span is an abstract extent whose real extent is approximated by inner and outer bounds, and its scope note contemplates the extreme case of a time-span with unknown beginning, end and duration that is still usable through relative chronology. Give the Joining and Leaving an E52 Time-Span carrying only P82 at some time within (outer bounds), and put the reason for the uncertainty in P79 beginning is qualified by and P80 end is qualified by rather than in a fabricated date. This case supplies two bounds for free. Below: the predecessor's own accession event. Above: the successor's first publicly observed striking of the flame. The annual lightings are ordinary instances of E7 Activity (P14 carried out by the keeper of the day, P4 has time-span that midsummer), and they are witnessed by the whole village even when the handover was not. State the ordering with P182 ends before or with the start of. That is the real gain here: the invisible transfer gets chronologically anchored by the visible exercises of the role, with no date invented.

4. The absence of witnesses is an epistemic fact, not an ontological bar. A CRM knowledge base holds statements representing propositions believed to be true in a reality by an observer (Modelling principles > Reality, Knowledge Bases and CIDOC CRM); nothing in E85 or E86 requires attestation, and the required P12 occurred in the presence of is satisfied by the two people who were there.

5. Where responsibility does bite is the word "unbroken". Gaplessness is a closed-world claim, and the CRM is monotonic: a later-discovered intervening keeper must be addable without retracting anything (Modelling principles > Monotonicity). So do not encode "unbroken" into the succession itself. Record the reconstruction as an E13 Attribute Assignment carried out by the documentation project, with P140 assigned attribute to the position, P141 assigned the keeper, and P177 assigned property of type. That is what E13 is for: it marks the maintaining team as neutral to the assertion's validity and registers whose opinion it was and how it came about (Modelling principles > Authorship of Knowledge Base Contents).

6. The right itself can be recorded, but not made to carry the chain. Instantiate E30 Right, typed with P2 has type, and attach each holder with P75 possesses, one right instance per holder, following Martin Doerr's reading on the list that where two people hold the same kind of right these are two different instances. Do not try to build the succession out of rights. E30 is a subclass of E89 Propositional Object and has no time-span, and giving right-holding a temporal extent is the one thing the SIG attempted repeatedly and never landed: issues 172, 335 and 343 were merged into 421, then into 408, which closed in April 2025 with the resolution to discontinue work on CRMsoc. Stephen Stead's CRMbase workaround in the archive was to use an activity that uses the right with a participating actor in a role, which serves for the annual exercise of the privilege but yields no succession. Two further caveats to pass to the project: E30's scope note says legal privileges, and E72 Legal Object warns that for conceptual objects the identity of the object or the method of its use may be too ambiguous to establish rights reliably. When the same question about traditional, non-legal rules reached the list in 2002, Martin Doerr's answer was that such a thing is a special case of a norm and he sketched a class for it that the CRM never acquired. So E30 plus a type is a serviceable label for the privilege, not a rigorous account of a customary norm; the succession of the role is the part that is rigorously modellable.

Bottom line: model the succession as events (E85 Joining and E86 Leaving over an E74 Group standing for the position), date them by bounds only, anchor those bounds on the publicly observed lightings, and attribute the "unbroken" reading to its author with E13. Nothing in the case forces a false assertion. The only false assertion on offer is gaplessness, and it is avoidable.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Confined to transfers of legal ownership, and its required P24 transferred title of has range E18 Physical Thing, so it cannot carry a right or an office. Issue 87 added to the scope note that an acquisition does not imply changes of rights in general. In t0507 Christian-Emil Ore proposed generalising P24's range to E72 Legal Object precisely so rights could be acquired; that was never adopted, and P24 still ranges over E18 in the current version.

Concerns physical custody, or legal responsibility for physical custody, of physical things (P30 transferred custody of, range E18). Nothing physical passes between the two fire-keepers; what passes is a position and the privilege attached to it.

rejected_alternatives.option: E63 Beginning of Existence / E64 End of Existence applied to the right
rejected_alternatives.why_not: This was tried on the list (t1019): create the right at one acquisition and take it out of existence at the next. George Bruseker and Stephen Stead both objected that the right qua conceptual object goes on existing as long as it is remembered, so the end of a tenure is not an end of existence. Using E64 for a handover would misdescribe the tenure boundary as the annihilation of the privilege.

This is the construct designed for exactly this gap: an n-ary relationship for a right held by an actor over a legal object, carrying the time-span that the P75/P105 triangle lacks. But the SIG resolved in April 2025 to discontinue work on CRMsoc, closing Issue 408, so it is not a safe target for a documentation project that wants its data to remain interpretable.

rejected_alternatives.option: Recording the succession only as free text with P3 has note
rejected_alternatives.why_not: It is the safest option against over-assertion but it discards the whole point of the exercise: the chain becomes unqueryable, the keepers unlinkable to the annual lightings, and the uncertainty undifferentiated from the facts. The E85/E86 plus fuzzy-bounded E52 construction gives the same epistemic caution in queryable form, with P79 and P80 as the place for the prose.

rejected_alternatives.option: E30 Right as the bearer of the succession, chained through P75 possesses or P105 right held by
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Neither property has any temporality, which is the substance of Issue 172. Every attempt to fix it (335, 343, 421, 408) ended without a CRMbase construct. A chain of right instances therefore cannot say who held the role when, or in what order.

siblings_considered.why_not: E21 Person is the class for the individual fire-keepers, and it is the very thing the position must be kept distinct from. If "the fire-keeper" were modelled as a person, the chain would have no subject that outlives its holders, and P107 would have nothing to hang on.

E8 Acquisition is the sibling a reader would reach for, since the case speaks of a transfer. But it is restricted to legal ownership and its required P24 transferred title of ranges over E18 Physical Thing; Issue 87 records explicitly that it does not imply changes of rights in general.

E10 Transfer of Custody would fit if the fire-keeper held an object on the community's behalf. Nothing is in anyone's custody: the role is a privilege to act, and E10's P30 transferred custody of demands an E18 Physical Thing.

The annual first-flame lightings, which E7 is proposed for here, take nothing out of existence. E64 is also the wrong tool for the handover itself, for the reason argued in t1019: the privilege as a conceptual object survives the end of a tenure.

E2 Temporal Entity is the phenomenon extended in time, and the handover is already one of those through E85/E86. What the undated moment needs in addition is E52, the abstract extent that can carry outer bounds via P82 while leaving beginning, end and duration unknown.

E73 Information Object is the right class for a written or recorded description of the custom, which the heritage project will also produce. The privilege of striking the first flame is not an identifiable immaterial item with a recognisable structure; it is what E30 was introduced for, subject to the caveat about the word legal.

E66 Formation is the class for the event that first established the fire-keeper position, and its scope note covers informal groups, so it would be the right choice if any founding were recoverable. It is not, and in any case E66 cannot record whose opinion the reconstructed chain is, which is the job E13 is here to do.

notes:
The office-as-group reading is the load-bearing move and I found it by accident: a mailing-list search for role succession turned up t1302, where the President of the Swiss Confederation is discussed as an E74 Group with one member at a time, which sent me back to E74's scope note where the clause about official positions independent of the current holder actually lives. That clause plus the E85 and E86 scope notes (inauguration into, and end of tenure in, an official position) is what makes the answer solid rather than improvised. Worth noting it rests on scope notes and one list thread, not on any issue closed on the point; and in that same thread Franco Niccolucci calls the Swiss example itself incorrect, though for a reason peculiar to Switzerland's collective head of state, not one that touches the office-as-group principle.

Two tool frictions. First, quote will not accept reference-document declaration chunks or section paths as source ids: both "Modelling principles > Reality, Knowledge Bases and CIDOC CRM" and "E52" were rejected as unknown sources, and docs --kind declaration prints no chunk ids, so the specification wording I rely on most (E74 on official positions, E85/E86 on tenure, E52 on unknown beginning, end and duration, E72 on conceptual objects being too ambiguous to establish rights) is paraphrased rather than quoted. Only the minutes chunk had a quotable id. Second, the rights-temporality trail is genuinely hard to follow through the tools: issues 172, 330, 335 and 343 merge into 421, 421 is declared a failed merging point and folds into 408, and 408 closes six years later by discontinuing the whole extension. Establishing that there is no CRMbase construct for the temporality of right-holding took five issue lookups, and the negative result is the single most useful thing I learned for this case.

One judgement call I want visible: I treat a village custom's fire-keeper as an official position in E74's sense. The scope note says positions regarded in certain contexts as one actor, which I read as satisfied by a community that treats "the fire-keeper" as a standing role, but a reviewer could reasonably say official implies an institution this case does not have. If that objection holds, the fallback is the E30 Right route, and then the honest answer to the project becomes considerably weaker, because right-holding has no time-span.
